title: Code Review Findings
description: Structured output schema for code review sub-agents

dispatchOutcome.description: What a persona returned: findings, empty, malformed, or never returned

disposition.description: What happened to an input finding: surviving, merged, suppressed, filtered, or rejected

overflow.description: Explicit marker that the complete evidence did not fit in one bounded entry

excerpt.description: Bounded excerpt retained when evidence must be shortened

reviewer.description: Persona name that produced this output (e.g., 'correctness', 'security')

harness.description: Harness that produced the artifact; populated by the parent orchestrator

findings.description: List of code review findings. Empty array if no issues found.

title.description: Short, specific issue title. 10 words or fewer.

file.description: Relative file path from repository root; absolute POSIX, drive-letter, and UNC paths are rejected

line.description: Primary line number of the issue

why_it_matters.description: Non-empty impact and failure mode -- not 'what is wrong' but 'what breaks'

autofix_class.description: Reviewer's conservative recommendation for how this issue should be handled after synthesis

owner.description: Who should own the next action for this finding after synthesis

requires_verification.description: Whether any fix for this finding must be re-verified with targeted tests or a follow-up review pass

suggested_fix.description: Concrete minimal fix. Omit or null if no good fix is obvious -- a bad suggestion is worse than none.

confidence.description: Reviewer confidence in this finding, calibrated per persona

evidence.description: Code-grounded evidence. At least 1 and at most 5 bounded entries; split evidence across entries or use an explicit overflow marker rather than silently truncating it.

pre_existing.description: True if this issue exists in unchanged code unrelated to the current diff

residual_risks.description: Risks the reviewer noticed but could not confirm as findings

testing_gaps.description: Missing test coverage the reviewer identified

confidence_thresholds.suppress: Below 0.60 -- do not report. Finding is speculative noise. Exception: P0 findings at 0.50+ may be reported.
confidence_thresholds.flag: 0.60-0.69 -- include only when the issue is clearly actionable with concrete evidence.
confidence_thresholds.confident: 0.70-0.84 -- real and important. Report with full evidence.
confidence_thresholds.certain: 0.85-1.00 -- verifiable from the code alone. Report.

severity_definitions.P0: Critical breakage, exploitable vulnerability, data loss/corruption. Must fix before merge.
severity_definitions.P1: High-impact defect likely hit in normal usage, breaking contract. Should fix.
severity_definitions.P2: Moderate issue with meaningful downside (edge case, perf regression, maintainability trap). Fix if straightforward.
severity_definitions.P3: Low-impact, narrow scope, minor improvement. User's discretion.

autofix_classes.safe_auto: Local, deterministic code or test fix suitable for the in-skill fixer. Examples: extract duplicated helper, add missing nil check, fix off-by-one, add missing test, remove dead code. Do not default to advisory when a concrete safe fix exists.
autofix_classes.gated_auto: Concrete fix exists, but it changes behavior, permissions, contracts, or other sensitive areas that deserve explicit approval. Examples: add auth to unprotected endpoint, change API response shape.
autofix_classes.manual: Actionable issue that requires design decisions or cross-cutting changes. Examples: redesign data model, add pagination strategy, choose between architectural approaches.
autofix_classes.advisory: Informational or operational item that should be surfaced in the report only. Examples: design asymmetry the PR improves but does not fully resolve, residual risk notes, deployment considerations.

owners.review-fixer: The in-skill fixer can own this when policy allows.
owners.downstream-resolver: Turn this into residual work for later resolution.
owners.human: A person must make a judgment call before code changes should continue.
owners.release: Operational or rollout follow-up; do not convert into code-fix work automatically.

return_tiers.description: Finding fields are grouped into two tiers, but both are returned together in one inline payload. Sub-agents do not write to disk; the parent orchestrator validates the complete return against this schema and persists it. The tier names describe how fields are consumed downstream, not separate transports.
return_tiers.merge_tier: Consumed during merge and dedup: title, severity, file, line, confidence, autofix_class, owner, requires_verification, pre_existing, suggested_fix (optional). Plus top-level reviewer, residual_risks, testing_gaps.
return_tiers.detail_tier: Consumed during synthesis, headless enrichment, and persistence: why_it_matters, evidence. Returned inline alongside merge-tier fields; a return omitting them fails validation and is recorded as a malformed dispatch outcome.
